Single-family homes exempt

quiz.q: What tragedy prompted Florida's condo safety inspection law?
options: Champlain Towers South collapse killing 98 people in Surfside
quiz.explanation: The 2021 collapse of Champlain Towers South in Surfside, killing 98 people, prompted Florida to enact mandatory structural inspections for aging condominiums.

laws.title: Flooding and Property Insurance Crisis
laws.subtitle: Florida's Insurance Market Collapses Under Climate Risk
laws.fullDescription: Florida faced a severe property insurance crisis as major insurers exited the market or dramatically raised premiums due to hurricane and flooding risks. Citizens Property Insurance, the state insurer of last resort, became the largest insurer in the state. Reinsurance costs and litigation reform were central policy debates.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; Citizens Insurance assessment risk for all policyholders
exceptions: Citizens Insurance state-backed coverage
FHCF catastrophe fund backing

quiz.q: What happened to Florida's private property insurance market?
options: It expanded to cover more risks
Major insurers exited leaving Citizens as the largest insurer
quiz.explanation: Major insurers exited Florida's market due to hurricane and flooding risks, making Citizens Property Insurance the state-backed insurer of last resort the largest in the state.

laws.title: Book Banning in School Libraries
laws.subtitle: Florida Libraries Remove Thousands of Books
laws.fullDescription: Florida's implementation of HB 1467 led to thousands of books being temporarily removed from school library shelves pending review by certified school media specialists. The law required review of all materials for age-appropriateness. Critics called it book banning; supporters called it protecting children. PEN America documented over 1,000 books removed.
laws.penalty: Criminal liability for school officials allowing unsupervised access to unchecked materials
exceptions: Classroom libraries with teacher review
Public libraries not covered

quiz.q: What Florida law led to thousands of school library books being removed pending review?
quiz.explanation: Florida's HB 1467 required all school library materials to be reviewed by certified media specialists, resulting in thousands of books being temporarily removed from shelves.

laws.title: Offshore Oil Drilling and Environmental Conflict
laws.subtitle: Florida Beaches vs. Federal Drilling Plans
laws.fullDescription: Florida's coastal tourism economy clashed with federal offshore drilling plans as the Trump administration expanded potential drilling zones in the Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico. Florida's Republican politicians diverged from the national party on drilling near Florida's tourism-dependent beaches.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for oil spills under Clean Water Act
exceptions: State objections to federal offshore leasing
Environmental review requirements

quiz.q: Why do Florida politicians oppose offshore drilling near their state?
options: Tourism-dependent beach economy that would be harmed by spills
quiz.explanation: Florida's Republican politicians oppose offshore drilling near the state because oil spills would devastate the beach tourism economy that drives billions in revenue.

laws.title: Flood Insurance Crisis and Real Estate Reckoning
laws.subtitle: Florida's property insurance market collapses under climate risk
laws.fullDescription: Florida faces an insurance crisis as major insurers exit the market, unable to profitably insure homes against increasingly severe hurricanes and flooding. Citizens Property Insurance (state-backed insurer of last resort) has grown massively. Premiums have tripled in some areas. The National Flood Insurance Program is deeply in debt. Florida's real estate market, built on the premise of cheap insurance, is fundamentally challenged by climate reality. Some coastal communities face managed retreat as insurance becomes unavailable.
laws.penalty: Lenders require flood insurance for mortgaged properties in flood zones regardless of market availability
exceptions: Historic structures in flood zones may get preservation-focused adaptation rather than retreat
Low-income homeowners receive subsidized coverage options through state programs

laws.title: DeSantis Culture War Policies and National Ambitions
laws.subtitle: Florida becomes laboratory for conservative social policy
laws.fullDescription: Governor DeSantis made Florida a laboratory for conservative social policy: book bans in schools, restrictions on gender-affirming care for minors, anti-DEI legislation removing diversity programs from universities, and the 'Don't Say Gay' bill limiting LGBTQ+ discussions in schools. DeSantis ran unsuccessfully for the Republican presidential nomination in 2024. The policies attracted businesses and conservative migrants while others left. Florida's rapid population growth from domestic migration continues despite (or because of) its culture war politics.
laws.penalty: School districts that violate book removal and curriculum restrictions face state funding consequences
exceptions: Higher education institutions have some academic freedom protections though limited
Private religious schools exempt from public school curriculum requirements

laws.title: Coral Reef Bleaching and Ocean Warming Crisis
laws.subtitle: Florida's Keys reef suffers record bleaching from marine heat waves
laws.fullDescription: Florida's coral reef — the only barrier reef in the continental US and third largest in the world — is dying from ocean heat waves. In 2023, ocean temperatures off the Keys reached 101°F (38°C) — among the highest ever recorded for ocean water. Mass bleaching killed significant portions of the reef. Scientists are conducting emergency coral rescue operations, moving heat-resistant coral strains to cooler nurseries. The reef supports $8.5 billion in economy and 70,000 jobs in Florida.
laws.penalty: Anchor damage to coral reef areas carries significant fines and potential criminal charges
exceptions: Designated mooring ball areas allow boat access without anchoring in reef zones
Scientific research diving has modified access to protected reef areas

quiz.q: What ocean temperature was recorded off the Florida Keys in 2023?
quiz.explanation: Ocean temperatures off the Florida Keys reached 101°F (38°C) in 2023 — among the highest ever recorded for ocean water — causing catastrophic coral bleaching and killing significant portions of the only barrier reef in the continental United States.

laws.title: Sea Level Rise and Coastal Property Insurance Crisis
laws.subtitle: Florida facing climate-driven insurance market collapse
laws.fullDescription: Florida's coastal real estate market faces an accelerating crisis as climate change drives sea level rise, intensifying hurricanes, and flood risks that are making insurance unaffordable or unavailable. Multiple major insurance companies have stopped writing new policies in Florida or withdrawn from the market entirely, leaving state-run Citizens Property Insurance Corporation as the insurer of last resort — now one of the largest property insurers in the US. Premium increases of 50-100% have hit Florida homeowners. FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program faces significant actuarial challenges in Florida. The fundamental problem is that property values in flood-prone areas reflect neither the true risk nor the long-term habitability challenge posed by rising seas and intensifying storms. Florida has historically been resistant to climate change-related building restrictions, even as the insurance market is forcing recognition of risk.
laws.penalty: Building without required flood insurance in flood zones can result in mortgage default triggers; local building codes carry permit and compliance requirements
exceptions: Some properties in flood zones have grandfather provisions under older maps

quiz.q: What has happened to Florida's private property insurance market due to climate risk?
options: Premiums have stabilized due to better risk modeling
Multiple major insurers have stopped writing policies or withdrawn entirely
The federal government has taken over all coastal property insurance
Florida has created a successful public-private reinsurance partnership
quiz.explanation: Multiple major insurance companies have stopped writing new policies in Florida or withdrawn from the market entirely due to hurricane and flood risks, leaving the state-run Citizens Property Insurance as insurer of last resort with ballooning exposure.

laws.title: Anti-DEI Legislation and Higher Education Culture Wars
laws.subtitle: Florida reshaping public universities through conservative legislation
laws.fullDescription: Florida under Governor Ron DeSantis has implemented some of the most sweeping changes to public higher education in any US state in recent decades. Legislation eliminated DEI (Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion) offices and programs at public universities, prohibited general education courses on critical race theory, gave the governor more power over university governance and faculty hiring, stripped tenure protections for professors, and created a Stop WOKE Act restricting certain workplace and classroom discussions of race. The New College of Florida was explicitly targeted for transformation from a progressive liberal arts college to a conservative alternative. Faculty departures have followed. DeSantis has sought to extend similar policies nationally through presidential advocacy. Critics argue the laws violate academic freedom and First Amendment rights; supporters argue they restore viewpoint balance to institutions they see as ideologically captured.
laws.penalty: Universities violating the DEI prohibition face loss of state funding; the Stop WOKE Act (partially blocked in courts) aimed at employers faces First Amendment challenges
exceptions: Private universities in Florida are not subject to the public university DEI restrictions

quiz.q: What was the Stop WOKE Act in Florida?
options: A law restricting foreign influence in Florida elections
Legislation limiting certain discussions of race in workplaces and classrooms
A regulation controlling social media content moderation
A law requiring balance in university hiring
quiz.explanation: Florida's Stop WOKE Act aimed to restrict certain discussions of race and identity in workplaces and classrooms, though courts have partially blocked portions of it on First Amendment grounds.

laws.title: Crypto-Friendly Regulation and Digital Asset Ecosystem
laws.subtitle: Florida positioning as America's crypto capital
laws.fullDescription: Florida has positioned itself as one of the most welcoming US states for cryptocurrency and digital asset businesses, with Governor DeSantis signing legislation prohibiting state agencies from participating in a federal CBDC (Central Bank Digital Currency) and establishing relatively clear regulatory frameworks for crypto businesses. Miami under Mayor Francis Suarez has actively courted crypto companies, hosting major conferences and attempting to create a city cryptocurrency (MiamiCoin). Florida has attracted crypto companies relocating from California and New York, seeking a less regulated environment. The state has significant fintech startup activity. However, the broader crypto market turmoil — including the collapse of FTX, whose founder Sam Bankman-Fried had significant Florida connections and had hosted events there — tested the crypto-friendly posture. Florida's regulatory framework attempts to balance innovation with consumer protection.
laws.penalty: State money services business licenses are required for crypto firms; federal regulations apply regardless of state law
exceptions: Some crypto activities may qualify for exemptions depending on whether they involve securities

quiz.q: What did Florida Governor DeSantis sign legislation to prohibit state agencies from participating in?
options: A federal Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)
SEC oversight of state-chartered crypto companies
quiz.explanation: DeSantis signed legislation prohibiting Florida state agencies from participating in a federal Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), reflecting concerns about government financial surveillance and a broader pro-crypto, limited-government stance.

laws.title: Insurance Market Collapse and Property Risk
laws.subtitle: Florida homeowners abandoned by major insurers flee state
laws.fullDescription: Florida's homeowner insurance market collapsed with dozens of insurers either becoming insolvent or withdrawing from the state. Major national carriers like Farmers and AAA stopped writing new policies. State-backed Citizens Insurance became the insurer of last resort with an unsustainable policy load. Average Florida homeowners pay three to four times the national average for insurance. The crisis reflects the uninsurability of climate-exposed coastal property and is reshaping Florida's real estate market.
laws.penalty: Mortgage lenders require home insurance; properties without insurance cannot be financed through conventional mortgages
exceptions: State Citizens Insurance provides coverage of last resort though with limitations
Properties inland may find more affordable coverage in private market

quiz.q: How much more do average Florida homeowners pay for insurance compared to the national average?
options: Three to four times the national average
quiz.explanation: Florida homeowners pay three to four times the national average for homeowners insurance due to hurricane risk and climate change, reflecting the growing uninsurability of coastal property.

laws.title: DeSantis Education Culture Wars
laws.subtitle: Florida leads conservative curriculum battle that spreads nationally
laws.fullDescription: Governor Ron DeSantis made education policy a national issue with laws restricting discussion of race in history (Stop WOKE Act), limiting discussion of gender identity in classrooms (Parental Rights in Education Act, nicknamed 'Don't Say Gay' by critics), and controlling AP African American Studies course content. Many of these laws faced legal challenges, with some provisions struck down. Florida's approach influenced conservative states and became a template for the 2024 Republican platform.
laws.penalty: Teachers violating curriculum restrictions face disciplinary action and license revocation; districts face funding consequences
exceptions: Private schools largely exempt from curriculum mandates
Higher education has different standards than K-12 under most Florida laws

quiz.q: What nickname did critics give Florida's law limiting discussion of gender identity in classrooms?
quiz.explanation: Critics nicknamed Florida's Parental Rights in Education Act the 'Don't Say Gay' law because it restricted classroom discussion of gender identity and sexual orientation in early grades, though the actual law text doesn't use those words.

laws.title: Hurricane Insurance Crisis Deepens
laws.subtitle: Florida's uninsurability threatens real estate market fundamentally
laws.fullDescription: Florida's property insurance crisis has deepened with major insurers withdrawing from the state, Citizens Insurance (state-backed insurer of last resort) swelling to unsustainable size, and average premiums three to four times the national average. The crisis reflects climate change making coastal Florida increasingly uninsurable at premiums homeowners can afford. Some economists argue large sections of Florida coastline will become effectively uninhabitable as insurance becomes unavailable regardless of price. New reinsurance legislation tried to stabilize the market with mixed success.
laws.penalty: Properties without insurance cannot receive conventional mortgages; unpaid assessments from Citizens Insurance surcharges apply to all policyholders
exceptions: Properties in higher elevations with lower flood risk find more affordable coverage
Cash buyers can own without insurance though lenders require it

quiz.q: What do some economists argue about large sections of Florida's coastline due to the insurance crisis?
options: They will become more expensive but insurable
They will require federal insurance backstop
They will become effectively uninhabitable as insurance becomes unavailable
quiz.explanation: Some economists argue that large sections of Florida's coastline will become effectively uninhabitable as private insurance becomes unavailable regardless of price due to climate change risk—a profound challenge to Florida's real estate market and economy.

laws.title: Everglades Restoration Comprehensive Plan
laws.subtitle: Restoring America's Largest Subtropical Wetland
laws.fullDescription: The Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan (CERP), a $10+ billion joint federal-state project, aims to restore the natural water flow of the Florida Everglades after decades of drainage and agricultural contamination. Florida law requires phosphorus levels in Everglades water to stay below 10 parts per billion. The state has ongoing legal battles with sugar companies over nutrient runoff that causes algal blooms and kills seagrass, harming the ecosystem that protects South Florida from storms.
laws.penalty: Agricultural operations face fines for exceeding phosphorus discharge limits; injunctions possible
exceptions: Existing agricultural permits during phase-in periods
Municipal stormwater systems under separate permits

laws.title: Opioid Prescription Regulations
laws.subtitle: Pill Mills to Pill Limits
laws.fullDescription: Florida became the epicenter of the US opioid crisis in the late 2000s, with 'pill mills' — pain clinics dispensing massive opioid quantities — operating in South Florida. Florida law now requires prescribers to check the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) before prescribing controlled substances, limits initial opioid prescriptions to three days (seven days in some cases), requires pain management clinics to be licensed, and mandates opioid dispensing limits. These reforms dramatically reduced prescription opioid deaths, though illicit fentanyl has created a new crisis.
laws.penalty: Medical license revocation; criminal charges for operating unlicensed pill mills; DEA prosecution
exceptions: Cancer patients
Hospice and palliative care patients
Post-surgical prescriptions with documented medical need

laws.title: Florida Farm Worker and Agricultural Labor Laws
laws.subtitle: Immokalee Workers Lead the Way
laws.fullDescription: Florida's agricultural sector employs hundreds of thousands of farm workers, many undocumented, who historically lacked basic protections. The Coalition of Immokalee Workers (CIW) pioneered the Fair Food Program — a worker-driven social responsibility model requiring major food companies to pay a 1 cent/pound premium for tomatoes and submit to worker-designed code of conduct with third-party monitoring. McDonald's, Taco Bell, Subway, and major grocers joined. Florida's 2021 minimum wage increase to $10/hour (rising to $15 by 2026) via ballot initiative also benefited farm workers despite agricultural exemptions in some other protections.
laws.penalty: Fair Food Program violations: suspension from the market; wage theft: civil and criminal liability
exceptions: Agricultural workers exempt from some FLSA overtime requirements
H-2A visa workers have separate federal protections

laws.title: Florida Stop WOKE Act and Education Wars
laws.subtitle: Curriculum Control in Schools and Universities
laws.fullDescription: Florida's 'Stop WOKE Act' (Individual Freedom Act, 2022) prohibits teaching concepts related to racial guilt, privilege, or systemic racism in workplaces and schools. Governor DeSantis also restricted AP African American Studies (later modified), removed thousands of library books, limited classroom discussion of sexual orientation and gender identity (Parental Rights in Education, 'Don't Say Gay' bill), and took over the governance of the New College of Florida. These policies created a national culture war over education. A federal court blocked parts of the Act as violations of First Amendment rights.
laws.penalty: Teachers violating curriculum restrictions: discipline; schools can face accreditation issues; state penalties for non-compliance
exceptions: Private schools under different standards
Higher education First Amendment protections limit enforcement in universities

laws.title: SB 1718: Immigration Enforcement Law
laws.subtitle: Florida's employer verification and immigration crackdown
laws.fullDescription: Florida's SB 1718 (2023), signed by Governor DeSantis, created one of the most restrictive state immigration laws: requiring employers with 25+ employees to use E-Verify to check immigration status, invalidating driver's licenses from other states issued to undocumented immigrants, requiring hospitals to ask patients about immigration status, and mandating local jails to honor ICE detainers. The law caused an estimated 10,000-40,000 undocumented agricultural and construction workers to leave Florida within weeks, creating labor shortages in key industries.
laws.penalty: Employers with 25+ employees not using E-Verify face fines up to $1,000/day; knowingly employing undocumented workers leads to license suspension; hospitals not collecting immigration status data lose Medicaid certification
exceptions: Employers with fewer than 25 employees are exempt from mandatory E-Verify
Emergency medical care cannot be denied based on immigration status under federal law

quiz.q: Florida's SB 1718 (2023) required employers with how many or more employees to use E-Verify to check immigration status?
quiz.explanation: Florida's SB 1718 required employers with 25 or more employees to use the federal E-Verify system to confirm employees' immigration status, expanding to all employers by 2024, with fines for non-compliance.

laws.title: Drug Free Zones and Mandatory Minimums
laws.subtitle: Florida's harsh drug laws and fentanyl crisis response
laws.fullDescription: Florida has some of the strictest drug laws among US states. Florida's drug-free zone laws (near schools, parks, churches) double drug crime penalties. Florida's trafficking mandatory minimums are severe: 400+ grams of oxycodone triggers mandatory 25-year sentence. Florida was an epicenter of the opioid/pill mill crisis in the 2000s-2010s. Florida voters approved medical marijuana (Amendment 2, 2016) and recreational marijuana (Amendment 3, 2024) but Governor DeSantis challenged the recreational implementation. Florida's Legislature enacted strict fentanyl trafficking penalties.
laws.penalty: Simple cannabis possession (20g or less): misdemeanor; trafficking cannabis (25+ lbs): 3-year mandatory minimum; cocaine trafficking (400+ grams): 15-year minimum; fentanyl trafficking triggers enhanced penalties with 25-year minimums for 7+ grams
exceptions: Medical marijuana patients may possess up to 2.5 oz of smokable cannabis
Prescription opioid possession with valid prescription is legal
laws.sourceLabel: Florida Statutes Chapter 893 – Drug Abuse Prevention

quiz.q: Florida's drug-free zone laws enhance penalties for drug crimes committed near what locations?
quiz.explanation: Florida's drug-free zone laws enhance drug crime penalties when the offense occurs within 1,000 feet of a school, college, park, community center, church, or other designated location — effectively covering large swaths of urban areas.

laws.title: Don't Say Gay Law and Anti-Trans Legislation
laws.subtitle: Florida's wave of LGBTQ+ restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Florida's HB 1557 (2022), labeled 'Don't Say Gay' by critics, prohibited instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity in K-3 classrooms and restricted it in all grades. Florida's Parental Rights in Education Act expanded these restrictions. Florida enacted SB 254 (2023) banning gender-affirming care for minors and restricting adult access to gender-affirming care. Florida removed LGBTQ+ topics from public library books. Governor DeSantis framed these as parental rights protections; LGBTQ+ advocates called them discriminatory.
laws.penalty: School districts violating the LGBTQ+ instruction prohibitions face loss of funding; healthcare providers treating transgender minors face license revocation; violations of parental rights provisions: civil and administrative penalties
exceptions: Federal employment protections apply regardless of state restrictions
Adults retain right to gender-affirming care (with significant restrictions on providers)
Private schools not bound by same provisions

quiz.q: Florida's HB 1557 was dubbed 'Don't Say Gay' by critics. What did it formally prohibit?
options: Classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity in K-3 (and restricted in higher grades)
quiz.explanation: Florida HB 1557 formally prohibited classroom instruction on sexual orientation or gender identity in grades K-3 and required that such instruction be 'age-appropriate and developmentally appropriate' in other grades — critics argued this effectively banned LGBTQ+ topics across the board.

laws.title: Anti-Press Legislation and Weakened Shield Laws
laws.subtitle: Florida has seen legislation restricting press rights and weakening defamation standards
laws.fullDescription: Florida has a reporter privilege under Florida Statutes Section 90.5015 but it is weaker than many states. In recent years, Florida passed legislation that could weaken defamation protections for journalists, including bills that would presume statements about public officials are false and remove the 'actual malice' standard for some plaintiffs. Governor DeSantis has been vocal against press coverage, and Florida passed laws restricting what teachers and media can discuss. The SB 1316 (2023) on defamation standards was signed into law. Florida also has a Public Records Act (Sunshine Law).
laws.penalty: Defamation liability risk increased by 2023 legislation; reporter privilege is qualified
exceptions: Courts have pushed back on some provisions; First Amendment federal protections still apply

quiz.q: What controversial change did Florida's 2023 SB 1316 make to defamation law affecting journalists?
options: Shifted defamation presumptions against media for some cases
quiz.explanation: Florida's 2023 SB 1316 modified defamation standards, shifting presumptions in ways that could disadvantage media defendants — part of a broader legislative trend in Florida that critics say undermines press freedom established by New York Times v. Sullivan.

laws.title: SB 7072 and Children's Online Safety Laws
laws.subtitle: Florida has multiple social media laws targeting platform power and child safety
laws.fullDescription: Florida passed SB 7072 (2021) prohibiting social media platforms from deplatforming political candidates — struck down by lower courts. The US Supreme Court's Moody v. NetChoice (2024) addressed Florida's law alongside Texas's, remanding for lower court reconsideration. Florida also passed the Florida Digital Bill of Rights (2023) and the HB 3 (2024) banning children under 14 from social media accounts entirely — the most restrictive age-based social media law in the US, challenged on First Amendment grounds. Florida reflects aggressive Republican state-level social media regulation.
laws.penalty: Platform violations can result in civil penalties; children's social media ban: platforms face fines for non-compliance
exceptions: First Amendment challenges ongoing; NetChoice Supreme Court case remanded

quiz.q: What age limit did Florida's HB 3 (2024) set for social media accounts, the most restrictive in the US?
quiz.explanation: Florida's HB 3 (2024) bans children under 14 from having social media accounts entirely — the most restrictive age-based social media restriction in the United States, going beyond the federal COPPA standard of 13 and challenged on First Amendment grounds.

laws.title: Florida's Financial Services Industry and Anti-CBDC Law
laws.subtitle: Florida is a major banking state that became the first to legally prohibit a federal CBDC
laws.fullDescription: Florida hosts a large financial services sector in Miami, Tampa, and Jacksonville. Florida became the first US state to pass legislation prohibiting the use of any Federal Reserve Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) as money in Florida (2023), a politically-driven law against the prospect of a 'FedCoin.' Florida's Office of Financial Regulation oversees state-chartered banks and financial services. Miami has become a major hub for cryptocurrency and DeFi startups. Florida has a large remittance industry serving Latin American communities. Florida's proximity to Caribbean and Latin American markets makes international banking significant.
laws.penalty: Florida financial regulations carry civil and criminal penalties; CBDC prohibition creates state law barrier
exceptions: Federal law would override the state CBDC prohibition

quiz.q: What unique political act did Florida take regarding a potential Federal Reserve digital currency?
options: Required the Fed to issue a digital dollar
Became the first state to prohibit a Federal CBDC as legal tender in Florida
Launched its own state digital currency
quiz.explanation: Florida in 2023 became the first US state to pass legislation explicitly prohibiting the use of any Federal Reserve Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) in Florida — a politically-driven law expressing Republican opposition to a potential 'FedCoin' and concerns about government financial surveillance.

laws.title: Florida DBPR Food Safety & Shellfish Harvesting Rules
laws.subtitle: Florida's warm climate creates unique food safety challenges especially for seafood
laws.fullDescription: Florida's Division of Hotels and Restaurants (part of DBPR) regulates all food service establishments. Florida's warm, humid climate creates elevated food safety risks, particularly for temperature control. Florida has specific regulations for its large shellfish industry — mollusk shellfish must come from approved, certified harvest areas and be properly labeled with harvest tags. Florida's Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) regulates food manufacturing and processing. Florida adopted the FDA Food Code standards with state modifications. Unique to Florida are regulations for raw juice and fresh-squeezed citrus at retail, and rules for the large kosher and halal food markets in South Florida.
laws.penalty: Food service violations: $100-$1,000 per violation; emergency closure for imminent health hazard; shellfish violations: loss of shellfish dealer license; selling food from unapproved source: criminal misdemeanor
exceptions: Farmers markets with certain exemptions for producers selling direct
Religious food preparation for congregation consumption
Cottage food producers selling non-hazardous foods directly have modified rules

quiz.q: What food safety challenge does Florida's tropical climate particularly intensify compared to cooler states?
options: Temperature control failures and accelerated bacterial growth in high heat and humidity
quiz.explanation: Florida's hot, humid climate significantly accelerates bacterial growth in improperly temperature-controlled foods. Foods that might be safe for short periods at ambient temperature in cooler climates can become dangerous much faster in Florida's heat, requiring strict temperature control compliance.

laws.title: Florida Animal Welfare — Shelter Reform and Cruelty Laws
laws.subtitle: Florida ranks high in animal cruelty reports; reform ongoing
laws.fullDescription: Florida Statutes Chapter 828 covers animal cruelty. Animal cruelty is a first-degree misdemeanor for neglect and a third-degree felony for intentional torture or killing. Florida's 2020 Animal Shelter Reform Law (HB 1199) required no-kill standards for public shelters — shelters may not euthanize animals if space is available and the animal is not medically hopeless. Florida also banned greyhound racing by constitutional amendment (Amendment 13, 2018), effective 2021. The state has an Animal Legal Defense Fund-rated inadequate shelter oversight, however, as enforcement gaps remain significant.
laws.penalty: First-degree misdemeanor: up to 1 year; third-degree felony cruelty: up to 5 years; aggravated animal cruelty: up to 5 years and $10,000 fine
exceptions: Agricultural and farming practices covered by separate statutes
Research animals under federal oversight
Pest control activities
Wildlife management by FWC

quiz.q: What did Florida voters approve in 2018 regarding greyhound racing?
options: A constitutional amendment banning greyhound racing
A license system for racing dogs
quiz.explanation: Florida voters passed Amendment 13 in 2018 with 69% support, adding a constitutional ban on greyhound racing. The ban took effect in 2021, ending decades of the industry in Florida.

laws.title: Florida Divorce and Alimony Reform 2023
laws.subtitle: Florida abolished permanent alimony in a landmark 2023 reform
laws.fullDescription: Florida enacted major alimony reform in 2023 — abolishing permanent alimony (which had been criticized as creating lifetime financial obligations with no endpoint). Florida now has time-limited alimony categories based on marriage length: bridge-the-gap (up to 2 years), rehabilitative, durational, and temporary. Durational alimony cannot exceed 50% of the marriage's length for marriages under 20 years. Florida is an equitable distribution state — marital assets divided fairly. Florida has strong protections for children in divorce — the Parenting Plan requirement mandates detailed co-parenting arrangements. Florida's 2023 reforms also created a rebuttable presumption of equal parental time-sharing.
laws.penalty: Contempt of court for alimony/support violations: fines and imprisonment; non-compliance with parenting plans: modification proceedings and possible contempt
exceptions: Prenuptial agreements can modify alimony
Cohabitation can be grounds for alimony modification
Chronic illness exceptions to durational caps

quiz.q: What major alimony change did Florida's 2023 family law reform make?
options: Florida required permanent alimony in all divorces
Florida abolished permanent alimony and created time-limited alimony categories
Florida allowed alimony to be paid in cryptocurrency
quiz.explanation: Florida's landmark 2023 alimony reform abolished permanent alimony — which could theoretically last for life — replacing it with time-limited categories. The most significant change was durational alimony limited to 50% of marriage length, ending the controversial practice of indefinite support payments in Florida.

laws.title: Florida Bert Harris Private Property Rights Act
laws.subtitle: Compensation for government actions reducing property value
laws.fullDescription: The Bert J. Harris, Jr., Private Property Rights Protection Act (F.S. § 70.001) provides landowners a cause of action when a government action 'inordinately burdens' property, even if it doesn't rise to a constitutional taking. Florida also has robust homestead protections under Article X of the state constitution, shielding primary residences from forced sale to satisfy most creditors. The state bans rent control via F.S. § 125.0103, with a narrow exception for housing emergencies declared by local governments.
laws.penalty: Compensation for inordinate burden on property value; homestead exempt from most creditor claims
exceptions: 180-day negotiation period before litigation
Emergency housing shortage exception for rent control
laws.sourceLabel: Florida Bert Harris Act & Homestead Protection

quiz.q: What unique protection does Florida's homestead law provide property owners?
options: Exemption from most forced sales to satisfy creditors
quiz.explanation: Florida's constitutional homestead protection (Art. X §4) shields a primary residence from forced sale to satisfy most creditors, one of the strongest such protections in the United States.

laws.title: Florida Unfair and Deceptive Trade Practices Act (FDUTPA)
laws.subtitle: State consumer protection and AG enforcement
laws.fullDescription: Florida's FDUTPA (F.S. § 501.201) prohibits unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts in trade or commerce. Consumers can bring private suits for actual damages (not punitive) and attorney fees; the AG can seek injunctions, civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation, and disgorgement of profits. Florida has also enacted specific consumer protections: Lemon Law (F.S. § 681) for defective vehicles, Motor Vehicle Repair Act, and Home Solicitation Sales Act with 3-day cancellation right. Florida's consumer protection division has been active against auto dealer fraud, debt collection abuses, and COVID-19 price gouging.
laws.penalty: FDUTPA: actual damages + attorney fees for private suits; AG: up to $10,000 per violation + injunction
exceptions: No punitive damages in FDUTPA private suits
Lemon Law requires manufacturer repurchase or replacement after reasonable repair attempts

quiz.q: Under Florida's FDUTPA, what types of damages can private consumers recover?
options: Actual damages only (no punitives) plus attorney fees
quiz.explanation: Florida's FDUTPA allows private consumers to recover actual damages (the difference in value between what was promised and what was received) plus attorney fees — but unlike some states, FDUTPA does not provide punitive damages in private suits.

laws.title: Stand Your Ground Law
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §776.013 — No duty to retreat
laws.fullDescription: Florida's Stand Your Ground law (2005) was the first in the US. It allows use of force, including deadly force, when a person reasonably believes it necessary to prevent imminent death, great bodily harm, or a forcible felony. No duty to retreat. The law gained national attention in the Trayvon Martin case.
laws.penalty: N/A — affirmative defense. Using Stand Your Ground incorrectly can result in murder charges.
exceptions: Cannot be the initial aggressor
Cannot invoke while engaged in criminal activity
Provocation can void the defense

quiz.q: When was Florida's Stand Your Ground law enacted?
quiz.explanation: Florida's Stand Your Ground law was enacted in 2005, making it the first state to codify such a law.

laws.title: Hurricane Building Code — Post-Andrew Standards
laws.subtitle: Florida Building Code — Nation's strictest codes
laws.fullDescription: Following Hurricane Andrew's catastrophic destruction in 1992, Florida enacted the nation's strictest hurricane building codes. All new construction must withstand wind speeds based on location (130–180+ mph coastal). Miami-Dade and Broward have even stricter standards. Impact-resistant windows and reinforced roofs are required.
laws.penalty: Contractors violating building codes: fines, license revocation, civil liability.
exceptions: Historic buildings may be exempt from some modern requirements
Renovations under certain cost thresholds
Mobile homes have separate standards

quiz.q: What major hurricane prompted Florida to overhaul its building codes?
quiz.explanation: Hurricane Andrew (1992) destroyed over 125,000 homes. Florida responded with the nation's most stringent hurricane building codes.

laws.title: No State Income Tax — Florida Domicile Rules
laws.subtitle: Florida Constitution Art. VII §5 — Zero income tax
laws.fullDescription: Florida has no state income tax, making it a magnet for retirees and wealthy individuals. Florida's domicile rules require 183+ days per year, Florida driver's license, voter registration, and Declaration of Domicile to establish Florida residency and avoid other states' income taxes.
laws.penalty: N/A — tax absence. Other states may pursue income tax if Florida residency not properly established.
exceptions: Federal income tax still applies
Intangibles tax eliminated in 2007
Corporate income tax applies to businesses

quiz.q: How many days per year must you typically spend in Florida to establish domicile?
quiz.explanation: Florida's 183-day rule (more than half the year) is the standard for establishing Florida domicile and avoiding income taxes from your former state.

laws.title: Parental Rights in Education Act — 'Don't Say Gay'
laws.subtitle: HB 1557 (2022) — Classroom instruction restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Florida's Parental Rights in Education Act (2022) restricts classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity in grades K–3 and requires age-appropriate instruction in other grades. Critics call it the 'Don't Say Gay' law. It has been expanded to higher grades. Teachers who violate it can be reported by parents.
laws.penalty: School districts face lawsuits from parents. Teachers may face disciplinary action.
exceptions: Individual student discussions about their own family not covered
School counselors may address student mental health needs
Libraries have some separate rules

quiz.q: What are the original grade restrictions in Florida's Parental Rights in Education Act?
quiz.explanation: Florida's HB 1557 originally restricted classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity in kindergarten through grade 3.

laws.title: Homestead Protection — Unlimited Dollar Exemption
laws.subtitle: Florida Constitution Art. X §4 — No dollar cap
laws.fullDescription: Florida has the most generous homestead protection in the US — a primary residence is protected from forced sale by most creditors with NO dollar cap. The homestead also limits annual tax assessment increases to 3% (Save Our Homes cap). This is why wealthy individuals like O.J. Simpson relocated to Florida.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent homestead claim: back taxes, penalties, possible criminal charges.
exceptions: Mortgages and federal tax liens can still foreclose
HOA fees can lead to foreclosure
Child support and alimony judgments may attach

quiz.q: What is the dollar limit on Florida's homestead protection from creditors?
quiz.explanation: Florida's homestead protection has NO dollar cap, protecting the full value of a primary residence from most creditor claims.

laws.title: Condo Safety Law — Milestone Inspections (Post-Surfside)
laws.subtitle: SB 4-D (2022) — Mandatory structural inspections
laws.fullDescription: After the 2021 Champlain Towers South collapse in Surfside (98 deaths), Florida passed SB 4-D requiring milestone structural inspections for condos 30+ years old (25+ years near coast) over 3 stories. A second inspection is triggered if serious deficiencies found. Reserves must now be fully funded.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant condo boards face personal liability. Lenders may refuse mortgages on non-compliant buildings.
exceptions: Buildings under 3 stories exempt
Single-family homes not covered
New buildings have 30-year grace period

quiz.q: What tragic event prompted Florida's SB 4-D condo safety law?
quiz.explanation: The June 2021 collapse of Champlain Towers South in Surfside, which killed 98 people, prompted mandatory structural inspections for older condominiums.

laws.title: Sea Turtle Protection — Coastal Lighting Laws
laws.subtitle: Florida FWC — Lighting restrictions May–October
laws.fullDescription: Florida hosts the largest concentration of loggerhead sea turtle nesting in the Western Hemisphere. Coastal properties must use turtle-friendly lighting (amber, red, or shielded fixtures). No artificial lights can shine on the beach during nesting season (May–October). Driving on beaches at night is restricted.
laws.penalty: Disturbing sea turtle nests: $100–$50,000 federal fine.
exceptions: Emergency vehicles may use lights when needed
Research permitted with FWC permits
Some grandfathered lighting in existing structures

quiz.q: During which months are Florida beach lighting restrictions strongest for sea turtles?
quiz.explanation: Sea turtle nesting season in Florida runs May through October. Coastal lighting restrictions are strictest during this period.

laws.title: Pill Mill Act & PDMP — Prescription Monitoring
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §893.055 — Must-access database
laws.fullDescription: Florida was the epicenter of the opioid epidemic, leading to a strict PDMP. Prescribers and pharmacies must check the database before prescribing controlled substances. The Pill Mill Act (2011) targeted the unregulated pain clinics that made Florida infamous. Florida was first to require PDMP registration.
laws.penalty: Prescribing without checking PDMP: license suspension, fines.
exceptions: Veterinarians have separate protocols
Emergency situations allow one-dose dispensing before check
Hospital inpatients may be exempt

quiz.q: Why did Florida create one of the nation's strictest prescription monitoring programs?
options: Opioid epidemic — Florida was home to 'pill mills'
quiz.explanation: Florida was the epicenter of the US opioid crisis due to unregulated 'pill mills.' The Pill Mill Act (2011) and strict PDMP addressed this public health emergency.

laws.title: Zero-Deductible Windshield Replacement
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §627.7288 — No deductible for glass
laws.fullDescription: Florida law requires comprehensive auto insurance to cover windshield replacement with NO deductible. This unique law has led to widespread fraud with glass shops offering incentives for customers to file claims. Florida accounts for a disproportionate share of US auto glass claims.
laws.penalty: Insurance fraud in windshield schemes: felony charges.
exceptions: Must have comprehensive coverage — not required by state
Deductible waiver applies to windshield only
2023 fraud reforms reduced scheme abuse

quiz.q: What is the deductible for windshield replacement in Florida under comprehensive insurance?
quiz.explanation: Florida law requires comprehensive auto insurance to cover windshield replacement with no deductible — unique to Florida and linked to widespread insurance fraud.

laws.title: Medical Marijuana — Amendment 2 (2016)
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §381.986 — Medical cannabis program
laws.fullDescription: Florida voters approved medical marijuana in 2016 (71%). Qualified patients with specified conditions can obtain a Medical Marijuana Use Registry ID card. Recreational marijuana remains illegal. Smokable marijuana was added by court order in 2019.
laws.penalty: Recreational possession under 20g: misdemeanor (up to 1 year, $1,000). Larger amounts: felony.
exceptions: Medical marijuana card holders may possess and use legally
Low-THC CBD oil allowed for certain conditions
Hemp under 0.3% THC is federally legal

quiz.q: What percentage of Florida voters approved Amendment 2 (medical marijuana) in 2016?
quiz.explanation: Florida's medical marijuana Amendment 2 passed with 71% of the vote in 2016, far exceeding the 60% supermajority required for constitutional amendments.

laws.title: Citizens Property Insurance — Insurer of Last Resort
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §627.351 — State-backed insurer
laws.fullDescription: Citizens Property Insurance Corporation is Florida's state-backed insurer of last resort. Due to hurricane risk and insurer exits, many Floridians can only get coverage through Citizens. Florida's Hurricane Catastrophe Fund (Cat Fund) helps private insurers. Insurance costs in Florida are 3–4x the national average.
laws.penalty: N/A — Citizens is a coverage source. Insurance fraud: felony charges.
exceptions: Citizens has eligibility requirements
Rate increases capped but being modernized
Floridians being 'depopulated' to private insurers

quiz.q: What is Citizens Property Insurance in Florida?
quiz.explanation: Citizens Property Insurance Corporation is Florida's state-backed insurer of last resort for property owners who cannot obtain insurance in the private market due to hurricane risk.

laws.title: Red Flag / Risk Protection Orders — Post-Parkland
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §790.401 — After MSD shooting
laws.fullDescription: After the Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting (2018, 17 deaths), Florida passed the MSD Act including red flag orders. Law enforcement or family members can petition courts to temporarily remove firearms from dangerous individuals. Florida was the first Republican-controlled state to pass red flag laws.
laws.penalty: Violating a Risk Protection Order: third-degree felony.
exceptions: Petition must be based on credible evidence of danger
Firearms returned after order expires (typically 12 months)
Subject may challenge the order in court

quiz.q: What event prompted Florida to pass its Red Flag law?
options: Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting
quiz.explanation: The Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting in Parkland (February 2018) that killed 17 people prompted Florida to pass red flag laws.

laws.title: Gambling — Seminole Tribe Compact
laws.subtitle: Florida Compact — Hard Rock monopoly on casino-style gaming
laws.fullDescription: Florida has no commercial casinos. The Seminole Tribe has an exclusive compact covering blackjack, baccarat, and sports betting. Pari-mutuel gambling (horse racing, jai alai) is licensed. Florida's 2023 voter-approved sports betting allows mobile wagering statewide through the Seminole Tribe.
laws.penalty: Illegal gambling: first degree misdemeanor. Running an illegal gambling house: third-degree felony.
exceptions: Tribal gaming on tribal lands under federal IGRA
Approved pari-mutuel facilities
Charitable bingo and poker tournaments with limits

quiz.q: Who has the primary rights to operate casino-style gambling in Florida?
options: The Seminole Tribe under state compact
quiz.explanation: The Seminole Tribe of Florida has an exclusive compact granting them primary rights to operate full casino-style gambling in Florida.

laws.title: Government in the Sunshine Law
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §286.011 — Strictest open meeting law
laws.fullDescription: Florida's Sunshine Law requires all meetings of two or more members of a government board to be open to the public. No decisions can be made outside of sunshine. Email exchanges between board members can violate the law. Florida's is among the nation's strictest open government laws.
laws.penalty: Violation: second-degree misdemeanor, nonfeasance in office, possible removal.
exceptions: Attorney-client privilege for legal strategy sessions
Certain security discussions
Some personnel matters

quiz.q: Under Florida's Sunshine Law, what triggers an open meeting requirement?
options: 2+ members of a board discuss board business
quiz.explanation: Florida's Sunshine Law is triggered when two or more members of the same board meet to discuss board business — even a casual conversation may require public notice.

laws.title: Public Records Law — Chapter 119
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §119 — Very broad public access
laws.fullDescription: Florida has one of the nation's broadest public records laws. Nearly all government records are public and must be provided promptly upon request. Records of public employees are public. Exemptions are narrow and must be explicitly stated. Florida is a model for government transparency.
laws.penalty: Wrongful refusal to produce public records: agency pays attorney's fees.
exceptions: Social security numbers, financial account numbers
Certain law enforcement investigation records
Medical records, juvenile records protected

quiz.q: What happens if a Florida agency improperly refuses to provide public records?
options: Nothing — requestor must file a lawsuit
The agency pays the requestor's attorney's fees
quiz.explanation: If an agency improperly withholds Florida public records and the requestor must sue to get them, the agency must pay the requestor's reasonable attorney's fees.

laws.title: Everglades Restoration Plan
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §373 — $16 billion restoration effort
laws.fullDescription: Florida is committed to a 30+ year, $16 billion Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan (CERP). Phosphorus levels in water flowing into the Everglades are strictly regulated (10 ppb limit). South Florida Water Management District manages massive infrastructure. Agricultural runoff (especially from the sugar industry) remains controversial.
laws.penalty: Discharging excess nutrients into protected waters: FDEP fines up to $10,000/day.
exceptions: Agricultural operations have negotiated Best Management Practices
Urban runoff gets different treatment timelines
Emergency discharges have separate notification procedures

quiz.q: What is Florida's phosphorus limit for water flowing into the Everglades?
quiz.explanation: Florida's phosphorus standard for water flowing into the Everglades is 10 parts per billion — a strict limit to prevent algae blooms and invasive plant growth.

laws.title: Felon Voting Rights — Amendment 4 (2018)
laws.subtitle: Florida Constitution Amendment 4 — Restoration for most felons
laws.fullDescription: Florida voters approved Amendment 4 in 2018, restoring voting rights to most felons who completed their sentences (not murderers or sex offenders). The legislature then passed SB 7066 requiring all fines, fees, and restitution to be paid first. This 'pay to vote' requirement was challenged but upheld.
laws.penalty: Voting while ineligible: third-degree felony (5 years max).
exceptions: Murder and felony sex offenses: still require Governor and Cabinet clemency
All financial obligations must be paid first under SB 7066
Federal civil rights restoration also available

quiz.q: Under Amendment 4, which felons cannot have voting rights automatically restored?
quiz.explanation: Florida's Amendment 4 automatically restores voting rights to most felons who complete their sentences, but explicitly excludes those convicted of murder or felony sexual offenses.

laws.title: Florida's 2023 Legislation Package — DeSantis Era
laws.subtitle: HB 1 (2023) & other bills — Conservative policy agenda
laws.fullDescription: Governor DeSantis signed a broad package of conservative legislation in 2023: restrictions on transgender medical care for minors, expanded school choice through universal vouchers, immigration enforcement measures requiring E-Verify for large employers, and limits on state investment ESG criteria. Florida became a national model for conservative policy.
laws.penalty: Violations of new laws carry varied penalties depending on specific statute.
exceptions: Federal preemption may limit some state provisions
First Amendment challenges ongoing for some provisions
Some provisions have delayed implementation

quiz.q: What major education policy did Florida expand with near-universal eligibility in 2023?
quiz.explanation: Florida's 2023 legislation expanded its school choice/voucher program to near-universal eligibility, allowing virtually all Florida K-12 students to receive state funds for private schools.

laws.title: Motorcycle Helmet Optional for Adults Over 21
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §316.211 — Age-based exemption
laws.fullDescription: Florida does not require motorcycle riders over 21 to wear helmets IF they carry at least $10,000 in medical insurance. Riders under 21 must always wear helmets. Florida's partial helmet law passed in 2000. Florida has among the nation's highest motorcycle fatality rates. Eye protection is always required.
laws.penalty: Violating helmet requirement: non-criminal traffic infraction, $30 base fine.
exceptions: Riders 21+ with $10,000 medical insurance exempt
Enclosed motorcycles may have different rules
Mopeds under 50cc have separate rules

quiz.q: Can a 25-year-old ride a motorcycle without a helmet in Florida?
options: Yes, if they carry at least $10,000 in medical insurance
quiz.explanation: Florida riders 21 and older may ride without helmets if they carry at least $10,000 in medical insurance coverage.

laws.title: Florida Non-Compete — Most Employer-Friendly in US
laws.subtitle: Florida Statute §542.335 — Restrictive covenants enforced
laws.fullDescription: Florida is one of the most employer-friendly states for non-compete agreements. Courts must enforce reasonable non-competes and modify (not void) unreasonable ones. Employers are presumed to have legitimate business interests. Florida non-competes are highly enforceable compared to other states.
laws.penalty: Breach of non-compete: injunctive relief (court order to stop working), damages.
exceptions: Non-solicitation of clients or employees has slightly different standards
Former employees who were laid off have stronger defenses
Highly technical or trade secret roles get stronger protection

quiz.q: If a Florida court finds a non-compete agreement unreasonable, what typically happens?
options: The court modifies it to be reasonable
The employee gets a 3-month free period
quiz.explanation: Florida courts typically modify (blue pencil) unreasonable non-compete provisions rather than voiding them — making Florida very employer-friendly.
